deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page is a draft of §16 of Riemann's Inauguraldissertation (1851), the Dirichlet-principle part. The previous page drafts the connectivity material on cross-cuts (Querschnitte) and boundary components. In the printed text, Riemann considers the functional L (Omega) = ∫_T [(∂α/∂x − ∂β/∂y)² + (∂α/∂y + ∂β/∂x)²] dT over admissible λ. He must exclude minimizing sequences or limits λ that are discontinuous along a line. The reading of the prose is tentative because the hand is hard.

PROSE (lines 1–8). It shall now be proved that λ cannot approach a function discontinuous along a line indefinitely while L stays bounded. Suppose λ is required to agree with γ outside a region T' enclosing the line of discontinuity. Then T' can always be taken so small that L exceeds any given bound. The comparison uses T and ϱ in the usual (local) coordinates adapted to the discontinuity line, with an area element like δT.

KEY ESTIMATE (mine, standard reconstruction). Use local coordinates s (arc length along the line) and p (normal distance), so that dT ≈ K ds dp with K bounded. Suppose λ jumps from λ₁ to λ₂ across a strip of width δ. By Cauchy–Schwarz,
  ∫_0^δ (∂λ/∂p)² dp ≥ (λ₁−λ₂)²/δ.
Hence
  L ≥ ∫ (λ₁−λ₂)² K ds / δ.
This can be made larger than any C by letting δ → 0. That is the written line "So können wir offenbar ∫(λ₁−λ₂)² K ds > C machen", once δ is suitably chosen.

SCRATCH COMPUTATIONS (lower half). These appear to test whether a discontinuity at an isolated point is likewise excluded. The next page speaks of discontinuities removable by alteration at single points.
(a) Polar functional on a unit disc around the point: ½∫∫_0^1 [(λ−λ₀)² + (∂λ/∂ϱ)²] ϱ dϱ dφ.
(b) Dropping the weight ϱ gives a 1-D model: ½∫[(λ−λ₀)² + (∂λ/∂ϱ)²] dϱ.
(c) With a parameter μ: J = ∫(λ−λ₀)² dϱ + μ∫(λ')² dϱ, and the shifted form ∫λ² dϱ + μ∫λ'² dϱ.
(d) The line "λ + μ ∂λ/∂ϱ" is evidently an attempt at the Euler–Lagrange equation. The correct form is λ − λ₀ − μλ'' = 0.
(e) Integration by parts, boundary terms dropped: ∫λ'² dϱ = −∫λλ'' dϱ.
(f) Weighted (genuinely 2-D radial) version, using ∂(ϱ ∂λ/∂ϱ)/∂ϱ = λ' + ϱλ'':
  ∫ϱλ'² dϱ = [ϱλλ'] − ∫λ ∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ dϱ.
  Radial harmonic functions satisfy ∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ = 0, giving λ = a + b log ϱ.
(g) The last line, λλ' + ϱλλ'' = λ·∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ, expands the integrand of (f). The side term ∫ϱλλ' dϱ is another piece of the same bookkeeping.

What this points to (mine). For a point singularity the radial Dirichlet integral ∫ϱλ'² dϱ can stay finite even for unbounded λ, e.g. λ = log(−log ϱ). So point discontinuities do not force L → ∞. This is consistent with the next page's remark about removable point discontinuities.
errors: The equation written as 'λ + μ ∂λ/∂ϱ' is not the Euler–Lagrange equation of ∫(λ−λ₀)² + μλ'². The correct equation is λ − λ₀ − μλ'' = 0. It is probably just an unfinished jotting.

In the chain ∫λ'² dϱ = −∫λλ'' dϱ = +∫ϱλ ∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ dϱ, the last expression is not equal to the previous ones. For the weighted integral the correct identity is ∫ϱλ'² = [ϱλλ'] − ∫λ ∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ dϱ. There is a sign slip and a misplaced factor ϱ; it is scratch work.
Boundary terms are silently dropped in the integrations by parts. This is harmless if λ vanishes at the endpoints, but that is not stated.
The written equation 'ϱλ'' + ... ∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ = 0' is garbled as read. The intended identity is presumably ∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ = λ' + ϱλ'', or the radial Laplace equation ∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ = 0.

results.what: A function discontinuous along a line (jump λ₁−λ₂) forces the Dirichlet-type integral L to be infinite, via the estimate ∫(λ')²dp ≥ (λ₁−λ₂)²/δ, so L ≥ ∫(λ₁−λ₂)²K ds/δ → ∞.
results.modern_name: Finite Dirichlet energy excludes jump discontinuities across curves (W^{1,2} functions have traces, no jumps); Cauchy–Schwarz / capacity estimate

results.what: Radial and 1-D model variational computations: the Euler–Lagrange equation for ∫(λ−λ₀)² + μλ'², integration by parts, and the radial operator ∂(ϱ∂λ/∂ϱ)/∂ϱ.
results.modern_name: Elementary calculus of variations / radial Laplacian; point singularities have zero capacity in 2-D
results.usually_credited_to: standard (Euler–Lagrange); zero capacity of points is implicit in Riemann's removable-singularity remarks

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the published dissertation's argument (§16) that line discontinuities make the Dirichlet integral infinite, plus routine scratch calculus. The ideas are known as Riemann's; only the drafting details are new.

checkable.asserts: The linear transition across a strip of width δ has ∫λ'² = (λ₂−λ₁)²/δ, the minimum given by Cauchy–Schwarz; it diverges as δ→0.
The last line λλ' + ϱλλ'' equals λ·∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ.

checkable.sympy: r,mu=symbols('rho mu',positive=True); f=Function('lam')(r); l0=Function('lam0')(r); euler_equations((f-l0)**2+mu*diff(f,r)**2, f, r)
checkable.asserts: The Euler–Lagrange equation of ∫(λ−λ₀)² + μλ'² is 2(λ−λ₀) − 2μλ'' = 0, not λ + μλ' = 0.
It equals 1: an unbounded function with a point singularity can have finite 2-D radial Dirichlet integral, so point discontinuities are not excluded by L<∞.
λ = a + b log ϱ solves the radial Laplace equation ∂(ϱλ')/∂ϱ = 0.

transcription_corrections: The line read as 'λ + μ ∂λ/∂ϱ' has the fraction written separately below. It is likely an incomplete Euler–Lagrange jotting, possibly meant as λ − μ ∂²λ/∂ϱ².
'∫λ^{*2} dϱ' is likely ∫λ'² dϱ or ∫λ² dϱ for a shifted variable (λ−λ₀ renamed). The superscript is unclear.

In the prose, 'Coefficient der Stetigkeit' is doubtful. The sense, from the printed §16, is that λ cannot approach a function discontinuous along a line ('längs einer Linie unstetige Function') while L stays finite.
The deleted '[-ϱ-]' in the first integral appears to be a crossed-out factor before (∂λ/∂ϱ)², with the weight ϱ dϱ dφ kept at the end. The leading '½' is likely written as '÷2' or '½'.
'∂λ ϱ(λ−λ₀)' at the top of the scratch area is probably a scratched-out start of a derivative or variation expression, not a complete formula.
